This piece goes directly to the text of the opinion and the dissent, pulls out the key language, and explains what the Court actually did—and why it matters. If you only read one thing about Callais, read the actual words the justices chose to use here. joycevance.substack.com/p/wh…

6/Later in the day Jim Comey was indicted—for the 2nd time—in a case that skates on even thinner ice than the one that was dismissed last year. The indictment is about this now-deleted Instagram post. DOJ says it's a threat of physical violence to the president of the United States. It sure looks like 1st Amendment-protected political speech, though.

5/DOJ moved to dismiss the case arguing she could only go to an executive branch agency—one impacted by Trump's firings—for relief, which of course, would have been a joke. On Tuesday a judge ruled she was entitled to go to fed'l court since Trump purported to fire her pursuant to Article 2 of the Constitution.

Tuesday was a big day for legal news. DOJ filed a bizarre pleading that reads, at points, as though it was written by Trump. And DOJ indicted Jim Comey for the second time. Neither one of those was the weirdest story of the day, though. Read on: 
open.substack.com/pub/joycevan...

We’re here because too many people stayed in the sidelines. In case that isn’t crystal clear, we can no longer afford to do that. Not any of us.

Put simply, Trump cannot be permitted to exclude broadcasters whose viewpoint he disagrees with. It would be the end of the free press: F.C.C. Orders a Review of ABC’s Broadcast Licenses www.nytimes.com/2026/04/28/b...

Fox News' David Spunt says he's been told by sources that Former FBI Director Jim Comey has been indicted over an Instagram post. That's where we are in 2026.

The vice president of the United States should not be weighing in on criminal prosecutions, let alone criminal investigations in progress. This is how banana republics function, taking out revenge on enemies via criminal “justice“ process. Politicians should stay out of prosecution.
